requirements.requirement: The system must validate that prescription data schema rejects records missing required fields (e.g., NPI, drug code, volume).
The system must accept and correctly parse valid prescription records that conform to the defined schema.
The system must successfully ingest and normalize a batch of prescription data into the internal data model.
The system must aggregate prescription data by provider (NPI) during pipeline execution.
The system must map normalized drug data to at least one condition (ICD-10) during ingestion or scoring.
The system must produce a normalized prescribing appropriateness score within a defined range (e.g., 0–1 or 0–100).
The system must return consistent scoring outputs for identical input datasets across multiple runs.
The system must expose prescription analysis results via the Evaluate Care API endpoint with expected response schema.
The system must return a non-200 error response when the API is called with an invalid provider identifier.
The system must handle empty or sparse prescribing datasets without crashing and return a valid but low-confidence or null score.
The system must log ingestion and scoring errors during pipeline execution for observability.
The system must execute unit tests for schema validation, ingestion, scoring, and API layers with passing results.
The system must execute at least one end-to-end integration test covering ingestion through API response.
The system must ensure LLM-assisted condition mapping produces deterministic outputs when provided identical prompts and inputs under test conditions.
The system must validate that LLM-generated mappings are constrained to valid ICD-10 codes.
The system must fallback to non-LLM mapping logic when LLM output is unavailable or invalid.
The system must ensure LLM outputs do not introduce unmapped or hallucinated drug-condition relationships outside known taxonomy.
The system must verify that LLM-assisted scoring inputs match the normalized data produced by the ingestion pipeline.
The system must ensure LLM processing latency remains within acceptable bounds for integration tests (e.g., under defined timeout threshold).
The system must confirm that disabling LLM components does not break the pipeline and results in degraded but valid scoring output.
